articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The United States will slap taxes of 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 countries accounting for 99% of U.S. imports, charging that they have inadequately enforced bans on goods produced by forced labor.
articles.title: Trump to impose double-digit tariffs on dozens of countries

articles.author: Sequoia Carrillo
articles.description: English teachers are excited to have a new adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey to use to get students excited about the epic poem.
articles.title: How to keep an ancient text interesting to students? Make it a summer blockbuster

articles.author: Rachel Treisman
articles.description: A council packed with Trump appointees is poised to rewrite historic preservation rules. Critics say that could help him build his D.C. arch faster — and endanger important sites across the country.
articles.title: Trump allies are poised to weaken protections for historic sites — not just in D.C.

articles.author: Claudia Grisales
articles.description: Four Republicans joined Democrats to approve the measure. And while it is not legally binding, the resolution represents growing frustration inside Congress over the war.
articles.title: For a 2nd time, House approves resolution to end the war in Iran in a rebuke to Trump

articles.author: Jan Camenzind Broomby
articles.description: Despite criticisms of a brain drain from China to the U.S., the awards come at a time when several high-profile Chinese scholars have returned home, some citing an increasingly hostile academic environment in America.
articles.title: In a first, Chinese woman wins the prestigious Fields Medal

articles.author: Carrie Johnson
articles.description: The former special counsel led two criminal investigations of President Trump and has been a frequent target of Trump's ire on social media.
articles.title: Republicans urge Justice Department to investigate former prosecutor Jack Smith

articles.author: Tahneer Oksman
articles.description: Grace Farris' book brings readers behind the med school scenes — documenting anxiety over loans, bouts of impostor syndrome, friendships forged in stress, and the ever-impossible work-life balance.
articles.title: Get into med school in the graphic memoir 'See One, Do One, Teach One'

articles.author: Joseph Kim
articles.description: Medical workers in a Nairobi clinic used an AI tool to check their work. A new study evaluates the result.
articles.title: This AI tool promises a 'second pair of eyes' to clinicians. Did patients benefit?

articles.author: Jonathan Lambert
articles.description: To get slightly ahead of the virus, health officials need to quickly identify people at risk of infection, a practice known as contact tracing. That's a challenge in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
articles.title: Why health officials do not have a good handle on the current Ebola outbreak

articles.author: Emily Feng
articles.description: After a Saudi nuclear power deal raised alarm in Israel, President Trump announced online that the arrangement is subject to the kingdom normalizing relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords.
articles.title: Trump says Saudi Arabia's nuclear deal hinges on the kingdom normalizing Israel ties

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Follow today’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian exports sent to the US will be hit with a 12.5% tariff as the US president imposes levies on more than 80 nations.
The Trump administration unveiled the latest tranche of tariffs for countries over their “failure to impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced with forced labour”.
This, in our view, makes no sense.
Forced labour is definitely something which needs to be combated around the world, so we support that objective.
We absolutely need to see the strait of Hormuz be open and for freedom of navigation to happen there, for commercial shipping to be allowed through, and we very much call on Iran to allow that to be the case.
We need to see a restoration to the normal global fuel supply chain because it’s having a significant impact around the world.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: eye health warning over GLP-1 drugs; victims of clergy abuse promised ‘full’ compensation by Christian Brothers

articles.author: Jonathan Yerushalmy, Lucy Campbell, Maya Yang, Vivian Ho, Taz Ali, Siraj Datoo and Adam Fulton
articles.description:
This live blog has not closed, you can read our latest story from the region here

Earlier in the US day, before Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said it had stopped three oil tankers from passing through the strait of Hormuz, Donald Trump issued this threat on his Truth Social platform:
From this point forward, any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by Missile, Rocket, Drone, or any other device or weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT, including those located next to, or in, the Capital City of Tehran.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East crisis is ‘getting out of control’, UN chief warns – as it happened

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Vivian Ho
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Trump to impose fresh wave of tariffs on more than 80 countries

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

By a vote of 214-208 lawmakers in the House passed a war powers resolution to curb the Trump administration’s military action in Iran, ahead of the lower chamber’s August reccess.
Four Republicans, Brian Fitzpatrick, Warren Davidson, Tom Barrett and Thomas Massie, voted yes, alongside all Democrats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats criticize Trump’s new tariffs as ‘end-run around the supreme court and Congress’ – as it happened

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Hannah Ellis-Petersen; produced by Saskia Collette, Alex Atack and Brian McNamara; executive producer Eli Block
articles.description:
South Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis-Petersen on the Cockroach movement – and the students driving India’s biggest protests in years
‘I’ve never seen this many young people out on the streets,’ says Hannah Ellis-Petersen.
For days, tens of thousands of Indians have been marching under the banner of the Cockroach Janta party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The ‘cockroaches’ marching on India’s government – podcast

articles.author: Gaya Gupta
articles.description:
Tariffs ranging from 10%-12.5%, taking effect on Friday, are US president’s latest effort to circumvent Congress
Just before a temporary levy on global imports was set to expire, the Trump administration issued a fresh wave of tariffs on more than 80 countries late on Thursday, ranging from 10% to 12.5%. The new tariffs take effect Friday morning.
It’s Donald Trump’s latest effort to continue imposing global levies without congressional approval, despite the supreme court ruling in February that found the US president had illegally used his executive power to implement his global trade policies. Trump has long maintained that the US has been paying more than its fair share in tariffs, and that increased duties are necessary to boost American manufacturing and jobs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What to know about Trump’s new tariffs on more than 80 countries

articles.author: Gaya Gupta and Shrai Popat
articles.description:
New tariffs to replace 10% global duty set to expire on Friday as administration cites concerns over ‘forced labor’
Donald Trump’s administration has ordered a fresh wave of sweeping tariffs on dozens of US trading partners to replace a 10% global duty that was set to expire early Friday morning – the latest attempt to instate aggressive trade policies despite challenges from the country’s highest court.
Starting Friday at 12.01am, the US will impose between a 10% or 12.5% tariff on more than 80 countries, which includes the United Kingdom, Mexico, Canada, Australia, India, China and the 27 countries that make up the European Union. It effectively replaces the blanket 10% tariff that Trump imposed in February, right after the US supreme court declared that his many of his earlier tariffs were illegal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump to impose fresh wave of tariffs on more than 80 countries

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
New York Times reports that list of those killed changed from 18 on Wednesday to 14 on Thursday
The Pentagon’s official online list of service members killed in the ongoing Iran war does not include the four soldiers who died during renewed fighting over the weekend, despite the fact that their names were included in a Pentagon press release on the formal transfer of their remains back to the United States on Wednesday.
A review of the current list on the Pentagon’s Defense Casualty Analysis System website shows that, despite having been last updated on Wednesday, the number of US military personnel killed during Operation Epic Fury, the Pentagon’s name for the US-Israeli war on Iran that Donald Trump launched on 28 February, remains at 14.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon list of service members killed in Iran war removes most recent four

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Defense attorneys question LAPD criminalist on third day of hearing to decide whether singer will stand trial
Blood stains on objects recovered from singer D4vd’s former Los Angeles residence probably came from Celeste Rivas Hernandez, the 14-year-old whose decomposed body was found in his Tesla last fall, according to testimony heard in court on Thursday.
Prosecutors say D4vd, born David Anthony Burke, fatally stabbed 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez last year to prevent her from exposing the sexual nature of their relationship amid his rising profile in the music world.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prosecutors say blood stains on objects in D4vd’s home probably of victim

articles.author: Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Airbus A350–1000ULR becomes most watched plane on flight tracking websites as Qantas tests new aircraft for its Project Sunrise

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Qantas’s new ultra long-distance aircraft has landed on Australian soil for the first time on Friday after a 19-hour test flight from France.
The Airbus A350-1000ULR, designed for Qantas to complete some of the longest commercial flights in the world, set off on a nonstop journey from Airbus’ manufacturing facility Toulouse, France on Thursday, destined for Melbourne.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Qantas tests new ultra long-range Airbus in 17,000km direct flight from France to Melbourne

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Sonam Wangchuk halted strike amid concerns about ‘possible violence’ in India as protest movement urges demonstrations across country on Friday over police brutality
Indian “cockroach” activist Sonam Wangchuk ended a 26-day hunger strike on Friday over an exam paper scandal that has spiralled into a wideranging youth-led protest against Narendra Modi’s government, with protesters continuing to call for the education minister to resign.
Wangchuk said on social media that he ended the hunger strike in Delhi in the presence of two federal ministers at the urging of scores of members ⁠of parliament, and after “a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country”. He did not elaborate on the talks but promised to lay out details in a video soon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India ‘cockroach’ activist Sonam Wangchuk ends hunger strike as protests spread

articles.author: Jon Henley, Ajit Niranjan, and agencies
articles.description:
Spain declares national emergency around Madrid, as marine heatwave sees some parts of Mediterranean Sea 5C hotter than normal
Brutal heat torching southern Europe has forced about 30,000 people to flee wildfires in France and Spain as a marine heatwave scalds the Mediterranean and researchers warn that “Dantesque” scenarios cannot be ruled out as infernos worsen.
A “particularly intense” wildfire on France’s southwestern Atlantic coast prompted the evacuation of more than 18,800 people, including thousands of tourists from campsites and holiday homes, as firefighters struggled to control the blaze.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands flee wildfires in France and Spain as temperatures reach extreme levels in southern Europe

articles.author: Josh Butler
articles.description:
Australia’s trade minister, Don Farrell, says tariff regime is unjustified and inconsistent with free trade agreement with US

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Donald Trump has hit Australian exports with new trade tariffs, claiming the country is not doing enough to combat forced labour, but the Albanese government has demanded he remove them immediately.
The United States announced on Friday morning (AEST) that many Australian exports now attract a new 12.5% tariff as part of a broader regime affecting dozens of countries. However the Albanese government says Australia’s three largest export categories – including beef and gold – will avoid the tariff hit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump hits Australian exports to US with new higher trade tariff over claims of ‘forced labour’

articles.author: Hayden Vernon
articles.description:
IRGC claims base in south-west England was used by US to launch bombing missions, making it ‘legitimate target’
The government has said the UK is “ready to defend itself” after Iran’s military warned that any bases being used by the US were “legitimate targets”.
The UK has allowed the US to launch “defensive” operations from British bases hosting American planes since the start of its war on Iran but has refused to help in offensive operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK ‘ready to defend itself’ after Iranian threat over US bases

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Burnham says ‘no one in government loses when power is shared’ as he revives Brown-era national economic council

It’s not just a No 10 in the north, it’s an engine for growth throughout the whole UK | Andy Burnham

Regional mayors are to be given a leading role in the UK’s economic policy, Andy Burnham has said, as he called the opening of No 10 North “the biggest rebalancing of power our country has seen”.
The new prime minister has revived the national economic council [NEC], first set up by Gordon Brown to put the government on a war footing during the 2008 financial crash, arguing that economic growth requires the same level of urgency, focus and collective action.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Regional mayors to take key roles in UK policy decisions as part of No 10 North plans

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Conservative leader is becoming more confident and forging a message for her party, but faces a new opponent 
“So, Andy Burnham seems like a nice guy.” Those were the slightly unexpected opening words of Kemi Badenoch’s first speech since the change in prime minister. But make no mistake: she was there to bury her opponent.
Even Badenoch-sceptics inside the Conservative party and farther afield agree the Tory leader is becoming more confident, and has been able to forge an increasingly coherent message for her party, one based on a promise of economic competence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kemi Badenoch ‘has to adapt’ her rhetoric to take on Andy Burnham

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
MPs and others condemn behaviour of CT Group, which offered cash for positive coverage of clients
A political lobbying firm secretly paying journalists for articles favourable to its clients is facing calls to reveal full details of the payments, after the practice was denounced as a dangerous “attack on democracy”.
MPs, senior lobbyists and transparency campaigners all condemned the behaviour of CT Group, the firm co-founded by the campaign strategist Lynton Crosby, an election guru previously hired by David Cameron and Boris Johnson.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lobbying firm pressed for details about payments to journalists for favourable stories

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Clinical assessments concluded Rudakubana could not be safely managed in prison, sources say
The Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has been moved from prison to a psychiatric hospital after clinical assessment, the Guardian can disclose.
He was transferred to Broadmoor high-security hospital from the category A prison Belmarsh this week after it was concluded that he could not be managed safely in a prison environment, sources confirmed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Southport killer Axel Rudakubana moved to Broadmoor psychiatric hospital

articles.author: Pippa Crerar and Rob Davies
articles.description:
Hospitality businesses call on Andy Burnham to cut VAT and extend help to hotels and restaurants
Pubs, clubs and live music venues in England will receive a 20% discount on their business rates bills as part of a £100m aid package but Andy Burnham has immediately faced calls to be more ambitious.
The prime minister said the measure, aimed at supporting the high street and easing cost of living pressures, would be fully funded, including through a review of relief for businesses deemed not to make a positive contribution to communities, such as vape shops.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Business rates cut for pubs, clubs and music venues in England only ‘a small move’, say critics

articles.author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
articles.description:
President’s remarks follow Houthi strikes on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and oil prices rising past $100 a barrel again
Donald Trump has said he is close to deciding whether to launch “a massive attack” against Iran, on a scale larger than strikes already witnessed during the months-long conflict with Tehran.
Speaking to the Axios news site, the US president said: “I am considering a massive attack. Bigger than ever before. I am close to making a decision. We are all set for it.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump says decision on ‘massive attack’ against Iran is close

articles.author: Thomas Graham
articles.description:
Valentín Lavín Romero is the 14th mayor to be murdered since Claudia Sheinbaum became president in 2024
A mayor was shot dead on Wednesday in the Mexican state of Morelos after having survived a previous assassination attempt earlier this year. He is the 14th mayor to be murdered since Claudia Sheinbaum became president in October 2024.
Valentín Lavín Romero, who was from the Green party, an ally of the ruling leftwing Morena party, was wounded at the end of January when hitmen shot him at a petrol station on a motorway.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mayor shot dead in Mexico months after surviving assassination attempt

articles.author: Jakub Krupa
articles.description:
Mykhailo Fedorov says only in his former post could he ‘combat procurement corruption and complete the army’s transformation’
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has offered a bit more detail on the new package of sanctions, saying they are “the largest round in four years,” and will “hit Putin where it hurts most.”
In a statement, she said:
“We have agreed on the 21st sanctions package against Russia. 
It delivers sweeping measures targeting Moscow’s financial system, its military-industrial complex and energy sector, that keep Russia’s war economy running. 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ousted Ukrainian defence minister refuses any other role in Zelenskyy’s government – as it happened

articles.author: Miranda Bryant Nordic correspondent
articles.description:
Swedish nonprofit alleges cost to repair replica was $6,000 but Universal – which made $264m on film’s opening weekend – has not stumped up
The Swedish owners of a Viking longship replica that features in the Hollywood blockbuster The Odyssey say they feel “forgotten” after film-makers allegedly returned the vessel damaged and failed to foot the bill for repairs.
In nearly three decades at sea, the warship Glad av Gillberga – based on a wreck from around 1040 found in Denmark’s Roskilde fjord – has successfully sailed the North Sea, the Baltic and even voyaged to Canada.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Owner of Viking ship used in The Odyssey says studio has not paid bill for damage

articles.author: Josh Butler
articles.description:
In a fortnight of rolling blunders, the One Nation leader digs deep into the Trump playbook of blame-shifting

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

There’s apparently only one thing to blame for Pauline Hanson’s string of bad headlines in recent weeks, from her decision to pal around with the far-right convicted criminal Tommy Robinson to her  description of domestic violence on Wednesday as a “two-way street”.
According to the One Nation leader, it’s of course not Hanson herself who is to blame.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pauline Hanson blames ‘fake news’ media for her bad press. But serious leaders have to own their actions

articles.author: Philip Oltermann European culture editor
articles.description:
Danny Boyle’s drama about the acquisition of the Sun and a four-hour Elon Musk documentary will premiere alongside new films from Martin McDonagh and Werner Herzog – but only one female director has a movie in competition
The Venice film festival promises to take a swing at media moguls of the print and digital era this year, with Trainspotting director Danny Boyle’s new film about Rupert Murdoch’s acquisition of the Sun and a new documentary about Elon Musk included in the lineup of the films for the festival’s 83rd edition.
In Boyle’s Ink, which will open the festival on the Lido on 2 September, Australian actor Guy Pearce plays compatriot newspaper tycoon Murdoch, whose purchase of the Sun in 1969 sensationalised the media landscape and transformed public life in Britain. The script is written by Olivier award-winning playwright and screenwriter James Graham (Dear England, Brexit: The Uncivil War).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Murdoch and Musk in the crosshairs at Venice film festival

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison
articles.description:
Far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir was among thousands who gathered at Jerusalem’s most sensitive holy site
Israel’s far-right minister of national security, Itamar Ben-Gvir, joined thousands of Jewish extremists who stormed Jerusalem’s most sensitive holy site on Thursday.
Escorted by armed police, they prayed, waved the Israeli flag and sang the national anthem in a provocative display of political power.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli security minister joins Jewish extremists as they storm al-Aqsa mosque compound

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
articles.description:
The men were convicted over alleged plan to stage coup and organise deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year
Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year.
Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin were sentenced to eight and 11 years in jail respectively. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in Angola for cultural and business activities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two Russian men jailed in Angola for terrorism and spying

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
articles.description:
September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences
The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement.
While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MoD cancels army training in Kenya over powers to prosecute British soldiers

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose, Joanna Partridge and Richard Partington
articles.description:
Sharp rise in oil price reflects fears Houthi militias could strangle Saudi exports as US-Iran fighting intensifies

How the Bab al-Mandab blockade threat pushed oil back above $100

The oil price broke above $100 a barrel for the first time in two months as a fresh escalation of the Middle East conflict threatens to compound disruption to global oil supplies.
The benchmark oil price rose sharply on Thursday, from $95 the day before, amid fears that Yemen’s Houthi militia could strangle Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea while US-Iran tensions over oil flows through the strait of Hormuz intensify.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oil passes $100 a barrel again and shares slide as Middle East conflict escalates

articles.author: Ushika Kidd
articles.description:
Pioneering study linking noise pollution to Parkinson’s finds 3% increase in risk for every 11.5dB rise in noise levels
Long-term exposure to road traffic noise is associated with a higher risk of Parkinson’s disease, the biggest study of its kind has found.
Parkinson’s disease is a progressive disorder in which parts of the brain become damaged over time, affecting movement and balance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Risk of Parkinson’s disease may increase with prolonged exposure to road traffic noise

articles.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
articles.description:
PM says ‘those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared’ as scandal spirals into widespread anger
Narendra Modi has vowed to set up “fast-track courts” to speed up the punishment of officials accused of leaking examination papers, as the Indian prime minister seeks to quell a youth-led “cockroach” protest movement that has rocked Delhi and posed one of the biggest challenges to his government.
In his first public remarks on the movement, Modi posted on X: “Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth … Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Cockroach’ protests: India’s Modi promises to punish officials over exam leaks

articles.author: Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Hackers access Australian customers’ names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and some bank account details, company says

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Origin Energy customers’ addresses, phone numbers and partial bank account data have been accessed in a hack, the company has confirmed.
The firm has 4.8m customer accounts in Australia, providing electricity, fossil gas, LPG and internet services to homes and businesses.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Personal and banking details among customer data stolen in Origin Energy hack

articles.author: Eva Corlett in Wellington
articles.description:
Dunedin will be the focal point, having last experienced such an eclipse in 1163 – before any humans reached New Zealand
Hotels are booking out two years in advance in the New Zealand city of Dunedin as it prepares for the region’s first total solar eclipse in more than 850 years.
At 4.17pm on 22 July 2028, the moon will pass in front of the sun, casting a roughly 100km-wide shadowy band across parts of southern New Zealand. Everywhere within that band – from tourist hotspot Queenstown in the west to Dunedin city in the east – will be plunged into daytime darkness for 2 minutes and 51 seconds.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Total solar eclipse books out hotels two years in advance in New Zealand city

articles.author: Olivia Bowden and agencies
articles.description:
Trump’s 50% tariff threat means there will be no ribbon-cutting celebration of Gordie Howe International Bridge
A planned joint US-Canada ceremony on Friday celebrating the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor, Ontario, is no longer expected to take place after Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on most Canadian goods.
In announcing the tariffs, the president accused Canada of unfairly discriminating against US automobiles, alcohol and dairy products, escalating tensions with one of the United States’ closest allies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada cancels joint bridge-opening celebration with US amid trade tensions

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
US secretary of state says international community should ‘join forces’ against authoritarian Ortega regime
Nicaragua’s congress, controlled by the country’s long-serving president, Daniel Ortega, has announced a “work plan” to implement the authoritarian leader’s order that the country should no longer hold elections.
The UN and the US strongly condemned Sunday’s announcement by Ortega, who has been in power since 2007 and, after a controversial constitutional change last year, now governs alongside his wife, Rosario Murillo, as “co-president”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nicaragua’s congress announces ‘work plan’ to suspend elections

articles.author: Emma Bryce
articles.description:
Researchers listening off the Caribbean island of Dominica found variations in the mammals’ audible clicks when marine traffic was close
Sperm whales produce a specific pattern of clicking noises when they hear the noise of boats, researchers have found. The pattern is so distinct that the scientists who identified it said they can now use it to predict when ships are nearby.
Researchers from Project Ceti (the Cetacean Translation Initiative), a non-profit research organisation working to decode sperm whale communication, spent four years tuning in on the calls of 15 sperm whales off the coast of Dominica.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sperm whales change ‘vowel’ sounds when boats are nearby, scientists discover

articles.author: Danny Vincent
articles.description:
Isabel Rose, 26, sentenced to six years for blackmail and perverting course of public justice over her allegations against British man
A British woman who reported being raped to police in Hong Kong has been sentenced to six years in prison for blackmail and perverting the course of public justice.
Isabel Rose, 26, from south-east London, travelled to Hong Kong in early 2024 to visit a British banker she had met while travelling in south-east Asia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British woman jailed in Hong Kong for blackmail after accusing banker of rape

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales and Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Foreign minister Penny Wong will deliver speech criticising China’s recent launch of a nuclear-capable submarine-launched missile

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Penny Wong will warn China that Australia and other neighbouring nations will not be bullied by its “provocative” actions, after its involvement in another “destabilising and dangerous” incident this week.
The foreign affairs minister – who will deliver the address on Thursday in the Philippines, where the 59th Asean foreign minister’s meeting is being held – will also caution world leaders against placing a toll on the strait of Hormuz after both Iran and the US threatened to do amid the protracted conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia to warn China it won’t be bullied by ‘provocative‘ actions as it builds military and nuclear arsenal

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Proceedings suspended as politicians call for Modi government to address police violence and education scandals
India’s opposition parties have shut down parliament in a protest calling for the resignation of the education minister, in solidarity with the new youth-led “cockroach” movement.
Opposition politicians, led by the Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi, gathered outside the parliament building in Delhi on Wednesday, many dressed in black and waving placards calling on Dharmendra Pradhan to quit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Opposition parties shut down Indian parliament in solidarity with ‘cockroach’ protests

articles.author: Raphael Rashid
articles.description:
Prosecutors seek a one-year sentence and heavy fine after chef garnished dish with insects not approved for consumption
Prosecutors in South Korea have asked a court to sentence the owner of a Michelin-starred restaurant to one year in prison for serving a dessert topped with ants, an insect not approved for consumption under local food safety law.
The request, made on Monday, also sought a 20m won (£10,108) fine for the company that runs the restaurant, Yonhap news agency reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michelin-starred restaurant owner in South Korea faces jail over ant dessert

articles.author: Gavin Blair in Tokyo
articles.description:
In April Japan coined new term kokushobi for days above 40C as country advises workers to wear shorts to the office to cope with stifling heat
Japan logged its first official kokushobi or “cruelly hot day” on Tuesday since the new term for when temperatures top 40 degrees Celsius was introduced in April. The Japan Meteorological Agency coined the new designation to warn the public of the heat dangers of days that were once freak weather events but have now become more common.
The central Japan cities of Gujo and Tajimi in Gifu prefecture, along with Toyota in Aichi prefecture, all hit 40C. Gujo’s 40C and Toyota’s 40.1C were all-time highs recorded at their respective weather stations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan records its first ‘cruelly hot day’ as cities swelter in 40-degree heat

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Maya Yang and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for US Breaking News email

US gas prices have continued to rise since the conflict with Iran resumed this month. According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), a gallon of fuel is now just over $4 – almost a dollar more than a year ago.
It comes as Brent Crude, the international oil benchmark, is now up by almost 2% to $90.92 a barrel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump announces new tariffs on generic drugs to take effect in 2028 – as it happened

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease
A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.
The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Thousands of people again on the streets of Delhi calling for education reforms despite police violence on Monday
Taru had come to the protest prepared this time. In one hand was an anti-government poster and in the other was a bicycle helmet. “We need to have protection in case Delhi police beat us up again,” said the 25-year-old, who stood among her friends. “We are not scared of them and we won’t run away, no matter what they do. We’ll stay here till they listen.”
On Tuesday, central Delhi still thronged with thousands of protesters, as an unprecedented expression of dissent against the powerful ruling Narendra Modi government showed no sign of abating.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement protesters show no sign of backing down

articles.author: Kat Lay Global health correspondent
articles.description:
Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well
One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.
There are 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs, and it will take “immense” amounts of work to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030, the annual report from five UN agencies warned.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthy diet too expensive for one in three people globally, UN report finds

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Incumbent Carlos Vila Nova hopes to defeat his former party and secure second term as independent
Voters in São Tomé and Príncipe go to the polls for a presidential election on Sunday as one of Africa’s least populous countries seeks to burnish its democratic credentials.
According to the National Election Commission, about 142,000 people are registered to vote in the tiny African state’s elections, approximately 15% of whom live in the diaspora.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: São Tomé and Príncipe heads to polls in tense presidential election

articles.author: Gaya Gupta
articles.description:
Tariffs ranging from 10%-12.5%, taking effect on Friday, are US president’s latest effort to circumvent Congress
Just before a temporary levy on global imports was set to expire, the Trump administration issued a fresh wave of tariffs on more than 80 countries late on Thursday, ranging from 10% to 12.5%. The new tariffs take effect Friday morning.
It’s Donald Trump’s latest effort to continue imposing global levies without congressional approval, despite the supreme court ruling in February that found the US president had illegally used his executive power to implement his global trade policies. Trump has long maintained that the US has been paying more than its fair share in tariffs, and that increased duties are necessary to boost American manufacturing and jobs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What to know about Trump’s new tariffs on more than 80 countries

articles.author: Gaya Gupta and Shrai Popat
articles.description:
New tariffs to replace 10% global duty set to expire on Friday as administration cites concerns over ‘forced labor’
Donald Trump’s administration has ordered a fresh wave of sweeping tariffs on dozens of US trading partners to replace a 10% global duty that was set to expire early Friday morning – the latest attempt to instate aggressive trade policies despite challenges from the country’s highest court.
Starting Friday at 12.01am, the US will impose between a 10% or 12.5% tariff on more than 80 countries, which includes the United Kingdom, Mexico, Canada, Australia, India, China and the 27 countries that make up the European Union. It effectively replaces the blanket 10% tariff that Trump imposed in February, right after the US supreme court declared that his many of his earlier tariffs were illegal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump to impose fresh wave of tariffs on more than 80 countries

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
New York Times reports that list of those killed changed from 18 on Wednesday to 14 on Thursday
The Pentagon’s official online list of service members killed in the ongoing Iran war does not include the four soldiers who died during renewed fighting over the weekend, despite the fact that their names were included in a Pentagon press release on the formal transfer of their remains back to the United States on Wednesday.
A review of the current list on the Pentagon’s Defense Casualty Analysis System website shows that, despite having been last updated on Wednesday, the number of US military personnel killed during Operation Epic Fury, the Pentagon’s name for the US-Israeli war on Iran that Donald Trump launched on 28 February, remains at 14.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon list of service members killed in Iran war removes most recent four

articles.author: Josh Butler
articles.description:
Australia’s trade minister, Don Farrell, says tariff regime is unjustified and inconsistent with free trade agreement with US

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Donald Trump has hit Australian exports with new trade tariffs, claiming the country is not doing enough to combat forced labour, but the Albanese government has demanded he remove them immediately.
The United States announced on Friday morning (AEST) that many Australian exports now attract a new 12.5% tariff as part of a broader regime affecting dozens of countries. However the Albanese government says Australia’s three largest export categories – including beef and gold – will avoid the tariff hit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump hits Australian exports to US with new higher trade tariff over claims of ‘forced labour’

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Vote from advisory group – whose members include people linked to peptides industry – likely to embolden RFK Jr
A panel of federal health advisers on Thursday narrowly recommended easing access to several peptides popular with wellness influencers and celebrities, despite warnings from government scientists that the chemicals have not been shown to be safe or effective.
In a series of votes, outside experts to the Food and Drug Administration advised the agency to drop current restrictions barring pharmacies from producing injectable peptides with names like BPC-157, TB-500 and KPV.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US health panel recommends easing restrictions on controversial peptides

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Late-night host discussed Trump’s claims of a rigged 2020 election, push for voting changes and new Canadian tariffs
Last night, Seth Meyers focused on Donald Trump’s claims that China swayed the 2020 election, new tariffs on Canadian imports and his attempt to impose voting restrictions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seth Meyers on Trump’s approval ratings: ‘Worse than Bush during the Iraq war’

articles.author: Alaina Demopoulos
articles.description:
People have found language for moodiest part of their menstrual cycles, and the right has seized on it
Emily Rae Detrick, a health coach, wants women to be more in touch with their menstrual cycle in its entirety. This, she said on an October episode of Culture Apothecary with Alex Clark, a podcast popular among “Make America Healthy Again” (Maha) adherents, is “a way that you honor God and the way we were created”. It also serves her self-assigned mission to help “make America fertile again”.
In the episode and on social media, Detrick speaks at length about the luteal phase, the 14-ish days between ovulation and menstruation when women are more likely to experience irritability, bloating and food cravings. If a woman does not get pregnant after ovulating, or so Detrick’s line of thinking goes, her body becomes upset. “During the luteal phase, the reason why your stress threshold is so much lower is because this is the time your body would be incubating a potential baby,” she said. No baby, and you might turn into a frazzled, nagging shrew.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Why do I feel crappy?’: women are learning about their luteal phases - and Maha is weaponizing it

articles.author: Zoe Williams
articles.description:
Anton Jäger has been lauded for his exceptional ability to make sense of these strange political times – and he’s only 32. The writer and academic explains why we’re living in an age of hyperpolitics
‘I am acutely conscious,” said Andy Burnham outside 10 Downing Street on Monday, “that I am the sixth person in the last 10 years to walk up this street.” It was good to hear him say it because, beneath all the cabinet gossip and rune-reading, there is a feeling of terror about the immediate future and also about ourselves, the electorate. Is this who we are now? Wildly enthusiastic one minute, seething the next; as passionate about the change we want as we are convinced that those who promise it are incapable of enacting it?
It is perhaps not surprising that Anton Jäger’s recent book, Hyperpolitics: Extreme Politicization without Political Consequences, is being read by Labour watchers and leftwing thinkers. As the New York Times wrote, it’s “among the best and most dazzling efforts to model the political present in all its maddening strangeness”. Still, I think Jäger was surprised to have his honeymoon interrupted so I could interview him about it. Life comes at everyone quite fast in a hyperpolitical age.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Meet the man whose groundbreaking book is being devoured by the left

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with David Smith and Rachel Leingang . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this year, Congress reached a depressing milestone: 86% of Americans, a record high, disapproved of its job performance. But this summer, there have been some signs that shifts are underway. On the left, House Democrats have just voted in unprecedented numbers to withhold military aid from Israel, and across the country, progressive candidates are running competitive primary campaigns that are energizing a base fed up with the status quo. On the right, Republicans are reeling from the sudden death of Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina senator and one of Donald Trump's staunchest supporters. Mitch McConnell, the former Senate majority leader, remains sequestered following a health scare in June, raising questions of if a changing of the guard might be underway there, too. Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by David Smith, the Guardian's Washington bureau chief and Rachel Leingang, midwest political correspondent, to discuss gerontocracy, transparency, the rise of the Democratic Socialists of America and just how much of an inflection point this summer might be for both parties


This page was amended on 23 July 2026. A previous version misspelled Lindsey Graham. 

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is US Congress finally on the verge of a change? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Late-night host spoke about president’s recent social media posts, including comments on the World Cup and Canada
Seth Meyers discussed Donald Trump’s most recent comments on the World Cup, including his claim that players don’t work hard enough.
On Late Night, the host spoke about a social media post from the US president where he thanked Rudy Giuliani’s son, Andrew, for helping to organise the tournament in the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seth Meyers on Trump calling Canadian wildfire cost incalculable: ‘So he didn’t write that post’

articles.author: Steven Greenhouse
articles.description:
To win in this year’s midterm elections, the party must highlight that Trump has made huge financial gains while millions struggle to make ends meet
If the Democrats hope to maximize their chances of winning in this November’s elections, there’s a subject they need to scream far and wide about: Donald Trump’s immense and unprecedented corruption. The Democrats need to make clear to every American that Trump has shamelessly used his second term to increase his wealth by an astounding amount – by more than $2bn – all while millions of Americans are struggling to make ends meet, their struggles made worse by Trump policies that have pushed up inflation and gas prices.
Every day through election day, the Democrats should convey loud and clear that America’s billionaire president has focused far more on making himself richer than on improving the lives of average Americans. Trump’s corruption and conflicts of interest are so vast and outrageous that many Americans have little idea how vast and outrageous they are: ranging from Trump’s making more than $1.4bn from crypto last year to granting pardons to criminals whose families have donated to Trump’s campaign to his sons’ investing in startup companies that receive generous help from the Trump administration.
Steven Greenhouse is a journalist and author, focusing on labor and the workplace, as well as economic and legal issues
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats need to hammer Trump on his unprecedented corruption | Steven Greenhouse

articles.author: Robert B Shpiner
articles.description:
Stephen Miller warned of a leftwing ‘cancer’ threatening civilization. As a critical care doctor, I have a response to his diagnosis
The presumption that US elections are legitimate died last week in Washington. It was 237 years old. It did not die of one wound. It died of three, inflicted in a single day, in daylight, on the record. And the country, running to the loudest of them, never examined the one most likely to kill.
In critical care we distinguish the mechanism of death from its cause. The mechanism was a Thursday. The cause was chronic, progressive and untreated.
Robert B Shpiner is a clinical professor of medicine in pulmonary and critical care at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Three speeches on a single day signaled a dying American democracy | Robert Shpiner

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Once Republicans’ favourite punchline, Joe Biden’s son is now building an online following by trolling JD Vance, taunting Trump and embracing the absurdity of US politics
What sort of longshot candidate do we reckon is going to run for US president in 2028? The Rock? Kim Kardashian? Kermit the Frog? US politics has become so debased that being rich, famous and a natural-born citizen (sorry, Zohran Mamdani) now seem to be the only qualifications required for a job in the White House.
Which is why you shouldn’t entirely write off murmurings that Hunter Biden might be interested in following in his daddy’s presidential footsteps. When asked by a Fox News reporter about Hunter’s 2028 odds last month, Donald Trump suggested Joe Biden’s prodigal son might “do well”. If other “basket case[s]” in the Democratic party could do well, Trump added, then Hunter probably had a shot. Various analysts appear to agree. “Could Hunter Biden run for office? Don’t rule it out,” a recent Times headline blared. The article quotes a Biden biographer saying: “With a character like Hunter Biden in a populist, social media-driven political environment, you have to never say never.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hunter Biden for president? Stranger things have happened | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Bhaskar Sunkara
articles.description:
The congresswoman can run a serious national campaign on the left and pull a movement in behind it. She should get in early
In the summer of 2018, almost no one thought Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez could beat Joe Crowley. Crowley was a 10-term incumbent, the fourth-ranking Democrat in the House, a man some thought would one day be speaker. A 28-year-old former bartender and democratic socialist was the longest of long shots to succeed him. But ever since she did, the political establishment has been trying to decide whether to take her seriously.
For a while it decided not to. The Missouri representative Emanuel Cleaver said the Democratic caucus did not need her “sniping”, while the then senator Claire McCaskill dismissed her as a “bright and shiny new object”. Ocasio-Cortez seemed to enjoy the response. Asked on 60 Minutes whether she wanted people to underestimate her, she said: “Absolutely. That’s how I won my primary.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez should run for president | Bhaskar Sunkara

articles.author: Sam Levine Zhara Keogh Michael Kalenderian Sarah Bertram
articles.description:
Donald Trump delivered a primetime address to the country on Thursday, claiming that declassified intelligence showed Chinese interference in US elections. The US president revived long-running attacks on election security, despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote, which he lost. The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims

Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fact-checking Donald Trump’s address on Chinese election interference – video

articles.author: Hosted by Jonathan Freedland . Produced by May Robson, Jacob Liebenberg, Ned Carter Miles and the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj .
articles.description:
The debate about how old is too old to serve in public office has resurfaced this week after the shock death of the Republican senator Lindsey Graham and the surprise return of Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old senator who published a photo of himself in hospital after a long absence from the spotlight.
With rumours continuing to swirl around Donald Trump’s health, why is it US politicians seem to cling on to power for so long?
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Alexis Coe, a presidential historian and columnist for the New York Times Book review, about whether the US is becoming a gerontocracy – and what can be done about it
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Are American politicians too old? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with Shrai Popat and Lauren Gambino . Produced by Meg Driscoll, edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this week, Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine, was accused by a former partner of sexual assault. Platner denies the allegations, but on Wednesday, he suspended his campaign, accusing the “political establishment” of tanking his candidacy. But this is only the most recent scandal to have surfaced around Platner’s campaign — over the past year, the oyster farmer and combat veteran was revealed to have a tattoo that closely resembled a Totenkopf (a widely recognized Nazi symbol), a long paper trail of racist, misogynist and homophobic posts on Reddit, and in June, the New York Times published allegations from three former partners about Platner’s “toxic” behavior in their relationships, including, in several cases, physical intimidation (allegations Platner denied).
As Democrats regroup and evaluate their dwindling chances to flip the Senate in November, hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian political reporters Lauren Gambino and Shrai Popat to ask why voters flocked to Platner, why they were reluctant to abandon him as the scandals came out — and what the whole mess says about who gets the privilege of political redemption.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why Graham Platner wasn’t the answer to the Democrats’ man problem – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Hayden Vernon
articles.description:
IRGC claims base in south-west England was used by US to launch bombing missions, making it ‘legitimate target’
The government has said the UK is “ready to defend itself” after Iran’s military warned that any bases being used by the US were “legitimate targets”.
The UK has allowed the US to launch “defensive” operations from British bases hosting American planes since the start of its war on Iran but has refused to help in offensive operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK ‘ready to defend itself’ after Iranian threat over US bases

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Burnham says ‘no one in government loses when power is shared’ as he revives Brown-era national economic council

It’s not just a No 10 in the north, it’s an engine for growth throughout the whole UK | Andy Burnham

Regional mayors are to be given a leading role in the UK’s economic policy, Andy Burnham has said, as he called the opening of No 10 North “the biggest rebalancing of power our country has seen”.
The new prime minister has revived the national economic council [NEC], first set up by Gordon Brown to put the government on a war footing during the 2008 financial crash, arguing that economic growth requires the same level of urgency, focus and collective action.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Regional mayors to take key roles in UK policy decisions as part of No 10 North plans

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Conservative leader is becoming more confident and forging a message for her party, but faces a new opponent 
“So, Andy Burnham seems like a nice guy.” Those were the slightly unexpected opening words of Kemi Badenoch’s first speech since the change in prime minister. But make no mistake: she was there to bury her opponent.
Even Badenoch-sceptics inside the Conservative party and farther afield agree the Tory leader is becoming more confident, and has been able to forge an increasingly coherent message for her party, one based on a promise of economic competence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kemi Badenoch ‘has to adapt’ her rhetoric to take on Andy Burnham

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
MPs and others condemn behaviour of CT Group, which offered cash for positive coverage of clients
A political lobbying firm secretly paying journalists for articles favourable to its clients is facing calls to reveal full details of the payments, after the practice was denounced as a dangerous “attack on democracy”.
MPs, senior lobbyists and transparency campaigners all condemned the behaviour of CT Group, the firm co-founded by the campaign strategist Lynton Crosby, an election guru previously hired by David Cameron and Boris Johnson.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lobbying firm pressed for details about payments to journalists for favourable stories

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Clinical assessments concluded Rudakubana could not be safely managed in prison, sources say
The Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has been moved from prison to a psychiatric hospital after clinical assessment, the Guardian can disclose.
He was transferred to Broadmoor high-security hospital from the category A prison Belmarsh this week after it was concluded that he could not be managed safely in a prison environment, sources confirmed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Southport killer Axel Rudakubana moved to Broadmoor psychiatric hospital

articles.author: Pippa Crerar and Rob Davies
articles.description:
Hospitality businesses call on Andy Burnham to cut VAT and extend help to hotels and restaurants
Pubs, clubs and live music venues in England will receive a 20% discount on their business rates bills as part of a £100m aid package but Andy Burnham has immediately faced calls to be more ambitious.
The prime minister said the measure, aimed at supporting the high street and easing cost of living pressures, would be fully funded, including through a review of relief for businesses deemed not to make a positive contribution to communities, such as vape shops.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Business rates cut for pubs, clubs and music venues in England only ‘a small move’, say critics

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
CEO Chris O’Shea defends Centrica’s plans as it reports rise in retail profits following focus on bigger margins
The owner of British Gas has claimed that most households would rather speak with an AI chatbot than deal with the company’s staff as it prepares to cut 1,300 jobs from its call centres.
Centrica, the supplier’s FTSE 100 owner, plans to cut 800 jobs as the company carries out a “targeted deployment of AI tools”, on top of the 500 cuts it confirmed last month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Customers prefer AI chatbots,’ says British Gas owner as 1,300 call centre jobs axed

articles.author: Hayden Vernon (now); Tom Ambrose and Vivian Ho (earlier)
articles.description:
New PM says no prisoners will be released under the policy until there is an urgent review of scheme
Kemi Badenoch is speaking in central London at the moment and is expected to say that Andy Burnham is “still thinking like the mayor of Manchester”.
“Going by what he’s announced so far, Andy Burnham’s ambitions for Britain are too small,” she was expected to say.
My message to British businesses is quite simple: to British businesses, to British innovators, to British investors: I will back you as your Chancellor, and I’ll back you in financial services, in technology, in retail, in industry, in all parts of the economy.
I’m just as concerned about the cost of business as I am about the cost of living.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics: Burnham pauses early prisoner release scheme due to start in September – as it happened

articles.author: Sammy Gecsoyler
articles.description:
Strategy will tackle ‘public health disaster’ that claims more lives than fire, flooding or knife crime
A national strategy to address the “public health disaster” of drowning has been launched in England – hours after two women died at an Essex beach, the latest in a surge of water-related tragedies.
Among the measures being considered are: providing every child in England with water safety education and swimming lessons; establishing how climate change can increase risks; and media campaigns to inform bystanders how to respond to a potential drowning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mission to ‘eradicate scourge of drowning’ after deaths surge across England

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Shalina Rahman, 42, and daughter Sameeha, 15, were on holiday in West Mersea and boy is believed to be family member
The teenage girl and woman who died in the waters off an Essex beach were trying to help a seven-year-old boy who had got into difficulty, police believe.
Family members identified the pair as Shalina Rahman, a 42-year-old British-Bangladeshi teacher who is married to a Bangladeshi politician, and her 15-year-old daughter, Sameeha. The boy, who police say was a relative, is on life support in a hospital in London.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Teacher and daughter die after trying to help boy, seven, on Essex beach

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Escalating Houthi warnings to ships carrying Saudi crude through the strait lead to fears of further price surge
A fresh front in the Middle East crisis opened this week, bringing a return of soaring global energy markets and stoking fears that the oil price could surge to $120 (£90) a barrel.
In a matter of days the price of Brent crude has jumped by more than 13%, breaching the $100 a barrel mark on Thursday after Yemen’s Houthi militias took aim at a new target: Saudi oil exports via the Bab al-Mandab strait.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How the Bab al-Mandab blockade threat helped push oil back above $100

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
Tribunal rules surveillance aimed at identifying Vincent Kearney’s sources was disproportionate and unlawful
A former BBC journalist has been awarded £20,000 in damages after MI5 and the Police Service of Northern Ireland unlawfully obtained data from his mobile phone.
A specialist tribunal on Thursday ordered the agencies to pay the compensation to Vincent Kearney for attempts to identify his sources while he was the BBC’s Northern Ireland home affairs correspondent.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ex-BBC journalist awarded £20,000 after MI5 and PSNI unlawfully accessed phone data

articles.author: Rajeev Syal and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Probation union and crime victims had raised doubts over plan to free 6,000 offenders across England and Wales

An early release scheme for thousands of prisoners paused by Andy Burnham after an outcry from victims could still take place this autumn, despite warnings by probation officers of potential chaos.
The prime minister ordered an urgent review into the proposed early release of about 6,000 prisoners, due to begin in September with an initial group of about 700, saying he wanted to “minimise risk to the public” and would not hesitate to make changes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prisoner early release scheme paused by Andy Burnham may still go ahead

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey, produced by Sam Gruet and Ned Carter Miles, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Frankie Tobi
articles.description:
Andy Burnham’s first week in office has seen him announce a range of measures to help people with the cost of living crisis, and scrap several of Keir Starmer’s big policies. 
But critics – including former Starmer ministers – are questioning how they will be funded and whether they go far enough. Pippa and Kiran look at what’s behind Burnham’s policy blitz.
Please keep sending your comments and questions to Pippa and Kiran at politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com
Read Kiran’s article on Andy Burnham’s communication style here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: All change please: Burnham rips up the Starmer playbook – podcast

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Analysis of NHS England data reveals stark impact of air pollution in deprived areas
Children living in the poorest areas across England are 40% more likely to be admitted to hospital for respiratory infections, an analysis of NHS England data shows, with experts raising the alarm on the impact of air pollution on young people’s health.
The analysis, based on data obtained via freedom of information requests by the charity Impact on Urban Health, revealed 1,941 out of every 100,000 children living in the most deprived fifth of England were admitted to hospital for respiratory illnesses in 2024-25.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Poorest children in England 40% more likely to be hospitalised for lung infections

articles.author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Selection of economist formerly at helm of green thinktank marks continuation of decarbonising Miliband era
In her first 48 hours as energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh was left in no doubt about the thorny policy decision at the top of her in-tray. Protesters from Fossil Free London met her outside her new offices dressed as firefighters holding placards reading: “We’re already putting out fires, don’t start new ones.”
The MP for Peckham – a radical economist who is outspoken about the climate crisis – is a surprising choice as secretary of state for energy and net zero for those who believe the speculation in Westminster that Andy Burnham wants to approve new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Who is Miatta Fahnbulleh, the radical-thinking new UK energy secretary?
